## What a workflow is

[Getting Started with Claude AI](../index.qmd) explains what Claude Code is,
[Setting Up Claude Code](../setup.qmd) installs it, and [Claude Code for
Research and Project Management](../use-cases.qmd) shows the kinds of work it
helps with. This section goes one level deeper: each page is a single, concrete
workflow you run from start to finish.

Three things hold across them all:

- **You own the specification.** Claude does not decide what to analyze or how
  to present it. You set the goal; it handles the execution.
- **The value is in the loop.** Because Claude Code runs tools on your computer,
  it writes, runs, reads the result, and fixes what broke, so you react to the
  outcome, not to every step.
- **Nothing lands on the first try.** The rhythm is always ask, review, adjust,
  repeat.

Throughout, share **structure and code, never raw data**. See [Prompt
safely](../use-cases.qmd#prompt-safely).

## The workflows

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### Inherited code

- [Revive and understand inherited code](understand-inherited-code.qmd)

Take code you didn't write and can't run, and have Claude get it running,
interrogate it against the data, and hand back what it does, what it changed,
and the questions you still need answered.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### Whole-project setup

- [Let Claude set up and run your whole analysis
  project](run-your-analysis-project.qmd)

Have Claude lay a project's foundations, put each stage behind one command, and
drive the multi-language chain across Stata or R, Python, and Quarto to a
rendered deliverable.
:::

## Contribute a workflow

This set is meant to grow, and the workflows worth adding are the ones someone
has already run more than once: a process you repeat, not a tool you build. If
you have one that holds up across projects, propose it. See
[Contributing](../../../CONTRIBUTING.qmd).
